messages:
ana: heads-up — int4 canary (raven-liteq) spiked on codepoint/quote fragmentation when prompts include emojis or non-ascii punctuation.
canary-bot: canary=raven-liteq-int4 parse_fail=1.0% -> 7.2% (24h)
peter: examples from the raw canary emits (trimmed):
```
{\"tool\": \"save\", \"args\": {\"path\": \"/tmp/note.txt\", \"content\": \"Note  reunin @10:00\"}}
{'herramienta': 'guardar', 'argumentos': {'ruta': '/tmp/note.txt', 'contenido': 'Resumen\u2026'}}
{\"tool\":\"save\",\"args\":\"{\\\"path\\\":\\\"/tmp/x.txt\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"\u6982\u8981:\u2026\\\"}\"}
```
josh: observed failure modes: 1) curly/smart quotes emitted instead of ASCII quotes; 2) keys translated to locale (herramienta/ruta); 3) args emitted as a single escaped string; 4) positional arrays occasionally used instead of objects. parser either rejects or maps to wrong tool.
irene: quick low-risk mitigations: 1) conservative postproc: normalize smart->ascii quotes, single->double, and iterative unescape when top-level looks like an object; 2) lightweight detector to gate postproc (look for non-ascii quote chars, single-quoted keys, or leading \"{\\\" pattern inside args); 3) add a one-line English schema anchor in system prompt.
leo: quant asks: try PTQ with \"quote-preserve\" seed or raise clip threshold for punctuation/subtoken ranges. also test int4+vocab-remap where ASCII double-quote is forced to be a single token.
peter: a couple of tradeoffs: postproc recovers many cases cheaply but can add 10-40ms p95 latency and a small mis-repair risk (flattening intended strings). detector reduces wasted repairs. anchor is cheap and helps but not complete.
josh: I'll prototype the detector + conservative unescape (only when stripped string starts with '{' and contains ':"'). aim to run in canary pipeline today.
irene: I'll run an 8k-sample sweep across en/es/ja with configs: fp16 baseline, int4 baseline, int4+anchor, int4+anchor+postproc. capture metrics: parse_accept, repaired_count, misrepair_rate, wrong_tool_rate, p50/p95 latency. posting results tomorrow AM.
leo: I'll coordinate with quant for a clip/seed ablation and try vocab-remap config.
peter: if postproc+detector recovers >90% with misrepair <1% we can enable for canary; otherwise keep affected locales pinned to fp16 and escalate PTQ.
a na: thanks all, quick triage appreciated :thumbsup:
